content.text: {"persuasion":"PERSUADED","support_scope":"FULL","rationale":"The book's core — faith as trusting faithfulness, i.e., reliance on God's unseen promise held steady through obedience — is carried better by the printed texts than the strongest specific rival (faith as purely receptive trust/fiducia, with faithfulness only a subsequent fruit). Habakkuk 2:4's underlying emunah is lexically 'faithfulness/steadiness,' not bare inner trust; Hebrews 11:8 fuses the two in one sentence ('By faith Abraham... obeyed'); James 2:22 says works 'perfect' faith, not merely evidence it; and the book — unlike the popular use of Eph 2:8-9 — prints and explains verse 10, the unit's own conclusion that the saved are created 'unto good works.' The book also pre-empts the counter's strongest text, Rom 4:4-5, by distinguishing wage-claiming works ('reward... of debt') from works that enact received faith, a distinction Paul's own contrast supplies. The counter cannot cite any supplied text the book's core fails to explain, whereas the counter must gloss emunah, Heb 11:8, and Jas 2:22 against their plain force. The accepted prior finding on Belief (received testimony submitted to; refusal to obey = unbelief) independently supports the same covenantal structure. The entry's secondary elaborations (works do not purchase; works enact and mature faith; faith without works is dead) are directly stated by Jas 2:17, 22 and Rom 4:4-5/Eph 2:8-10, so the full entry is supported.","book_core_identification":"Faith is trusting faithfulness: reliance on God's unseen promise in which the steadiness of obedience is constitutive of the faith itself (emunah), not merely a downstream consequence — trust and fidelity fused in one disposition held through delay and testing.","book_secondary_elaborations":["Works do not purchase the promise (grace excludes wage-claim works, Rom 4:4-5; Eph 2:8-9)","Works enact faith and bring it to maturity ('by works was faith made perfect,' Jas 2:22)","Faith without works is dead (Jas 2:17)","Hebrews 11:1's 'evidence' is read as proof produced in the life — visible obedience standing in where sight is denied","Emunah's first appearance (Moses' steady hands, Ex 17:12) as the picture of faithfulness","Faith is one office among four (love, knowing, faith, belief) of a single covenant response"],"strongest_counter_interpretation":"Classic Reformed/evangelical reading: faith is exclusively receptive trust (fiducia) in God's promise and Christ's work — the empty hand that receives justification. Faithfulness and obedient works are the necessary FRUIT of faith but are categorically distinct from it; defining faith as 'faithfulness held through obedience' confuses the instrument of justification with its results. Rom 4:4-5 is the proof: the one justified is precisely 'him that worketh not, but believeth,' so working cannot be internal to faith's definition; James 2 means only that dead faith is exposed by absent fruit, not that works perfect faith constitutively.","counter_core_identification":"Faith is bare receptive trust in God/Christ, formally distinct from faithfulness and obedience, which are consequences of faith rather than components of it.","counter_relation_to_book_core":"CONTRADICTS","material_core_denial":"The counter denies that obedient steadiness (faithfulness) is constitutive of faith itself, asserting instead that faith is complete as inward trust prior to and apart from any enacted fidelity; both definitions cannot be true of the same referent.","counter_case":["Rom 4:5 defines the justified man as one 'that worketh not, but believeth' — faith is set in explicit antithesis to working, favoring a purely receptive definition","Eph 2:8-9 says salvation through faith is 'not of works,' suggesting works stand outside faith's definition","Rom 10:17 and the fiducia tradition treat faith as arising from hearing and resting inwardly on the promise; Heb 11:1 (hypostasis/elenchos) is standardly read as inner assurance and conviction, not produced external evidence","James 2 can be read as faith being demonstrated (not constituted or perfected in essence) by works — dead faith is counterfeit faith, so works are diagnostic, not definitional"],"book_explanatory_advantages":["Hab 2:4's emunah lexically means faithfulness/steadiness (its first use is Moses' steady hands, Ex 17:12); the counter must posit a semantic shift the printed text does not signal","Heb 11:8 places obedience inside the act of faith itself ('By faith Abraham... obeyed; and he went out'), and all of Hebrews 11 catalogs visible acts as the exercise of faith","Jas 2:22 says faith 'wrought WITH his works, and BY works was faith made perfect' — works as co-workers and perfecters of faith, stronger than the counter's merely evidential gloss","The book explains the whole Eph 2:8-10 unit including v.10 ('created in Christ Jesus unto good works... that we should walk in them'), where the counter's proof-text use stops at v.9","The book harmonizes Paul and James without strain: Rom 4:4-5 excludes wage-claim works, Jas 2 requires enacting works — two different senses of 'works' distinguished by the texts themselves","Coheres with the accepted prior finding that saving belief is received testimony submitted to, with refusal to obey constituting unbelief (Heb 3:18-19 pattern)"],"counter_explanatory_advantages":["Rom 4:5's 'to him that worketh not, but believeth' reads most naturally in isolation as defining faith against any working","Preserves a clean systematic distinction between justification's instrument and sanctification's fruit, guarding against works-righteousness","Heb 11:1's hypostasis/elenchos as inner 'assurance/conviction' is the majority lexical reading, more natural than 'evidence produced in the life'"],"evidence_book_core_cannot_explain":[],"comparative_winner":"BOOK","decisive_sources":["Habakkuk 2:4 (emunah = faithfulness/steadiness; cf. Exodus 17:12)","Hebrews 11:8 (obedience internal to the act of faith)","James 2:17, 22 (faith perfected by works; dead without them)","Ephesians 2:8-10 read as a unit (grace-given faith issuing necessarily in ordained works)","Romans 4:4-5 (book's own safeguard: works excluded as wage-claim, not as enactment)","Prior accepted finding on Belief (2026-07-12-belief-v8-revised, FULL)"],"unresolved_objections":["Romans 4:5's antithesis ('worketh not, but believeth') fits a purely receptive definition more naturally on a verse-local reading; the book's wage-claim/enactment distinction resolves it but is an inference, not stated in the verse","The book's gloss of Heb 11:1 'evidence' as proof produced in the observable life is contestable; hypostasis/elenchos are standardly taken as inner assurance and conviction","The systematic worry that making faithfulness constitutive of faith blurs the instrument of justification with its fruits is answered by the entry's 'works do not purchase' clause but not fully adjudicated against the Reformed ordo salutis"],"confidence":"high"}
